title: Cells architecture
caveat: Capabilities vary by model, and whole-cell integration is ongoing. No single run uses every part drawn here.

statuses.label: Qualified or judged
statuses.description: Numerically qualified (a registered protocol passed) or judged (used in a registered experiment), in its declared scope.

statuses.label: Implemented and guarded
statuses.description: On main with its tests and guards: the plan's 'implemented' and 'guarded' levels. Not yet qualified by a registered protocol.

statuses.label: Established
statuses.description: Built earlier and in routine use: older model families and shared infrastructure. Scope and evidence are in each guide.

statuses.label: Designed
statuses.description: A design or protocol is written or accepted; the code is not on main.

statuses.label: Planned
statuses.description: Named in the plan or roadmap; not started.

statuses.label: Failed qualification
statuses.description: Built, then failed its registered qualification. Kept as evidence and not relied on.

statuses.label: External reference
statuses.description: Outside the engine: a reference simulator or data set, run out of process and compared through saved outputs.

representations.label: Simulated
representations.description: The engine evolves this state step by step, with material, charge and energy accounted for.

representations.label: Modelled in aggregate
representations.description: Represented as a population, count or rate law, not as individual molecules. Shapes drawn for it are illustrations.

representations.label: Prescribed
representations.description: Happens on a schedule the experiment sets; the cell does not decide it.

representations.label: Illustration only
representations.description: Drawn for orientation. Nothing in the engine stands behind it yet.

model_groups.label: Composite tissue model
model_groups.description: resolved_pump_composite@1: the pump tissue model's own step plus declared operators. These parts run together in one model today.

model_groups.label: Earlier tissue families
model_groups.description: The older resolved-tissue families, one module per feature combination. Calcium, fuel, mitochondria, regulation and repair run together here.

model_groups.label: Separate engines
model_groups.description: Models that run on their own: protein-cage assembly, vertex mechanics and the regulatory circuits.

layers.label: Execution
layers.description: How a definition becomes a checked, restartable run.

layers.label: Numerics
layers.description: Time stepping, field solves and long-time methods.

layers.label: Shared state
layers.description: The entities that own physical state. Mechanisms that affect the same thing change the same state.

layers.label: Physical laws
layers.description: Transport, kinetics, chemistry, geometry and mechanics, one law per module.

layers.label: Models
layers.description: Versioned model families built from the laws.

layers.label: Operators
layers.description: Laws declared as operators of the composite tissue model.

layers.label: Experiments
layers.description: Clients of the engine: parity checks, morphogenesis, division and heredity.

layers.label: References and validation
layers.description: Outside the engine: reference simulators run out of process, independent reference solutions and the test gate.

layers.label: Plan gates
layers.description: The current plan's gates, in order, from docs/CURRENT_PLAN.md.

components.label: CPU, float64
components.plain: Every model runs on ordinary processors in double precision. These runs are the reference that GPU runs are checked against.

components.label: NVIDIA L4 GPU
components.plain: One GPU runs many independent worlds at once. All 12 BETSE parity protocols also pass on it, under registered GPU variants.

components.label: Ensemble workers
components.plain: Workers take batches of independent simulations from a shared queue, one persistent process per GPU.

components.label: JUPITER GH200
components.plain: A supercomputer allocation of 10,000 GPU-hours. The recipe and runbook are ready; nothing has run there, and its speed is unmeasured.

components.label: One world across GPUs
components.plain: Splitting one large interacting tissue across several devices. No code does this; it is added only if single-device measurements justify it.

components.label: Command line
components.plain: The command that runs a model from a configuration file and writes its results and checkpoints.

components.label: Definitions
components.plain: Each run is declared as data: the model, the experiment and how to execute it. Definitions are checked before anything runs.

components.label: Model registry
components.plain: Finds the model code for a definition. Today it is an ordered chain of type checks.

components.label: Declarative registry
components.plain: One table saying how each model takes part in parsing, saving, controls, execution and checkpoints.

components.label: State and resources
components.plain: State is held as explicit arrays with fixed capacities and masks; memory needs are estimated before a run starts.

components.label: Schedules and phases
components.plain: Timed changes an experiment makes, such as blocking a pump or a junction, applied at exact times.

components.label: Single-world runner
components.plain: Runs one world step by step with every check, in bounded windows. A reference path.

components.label: Guarded batch
components.plain: Runs many independent worlds, each on its own clock, with rows checked on the host.

components.label: Batch windows
components.plain: Runs cohorts of worlds in bounded rounds, with complete cohort checkpoints.

components.label: Vector windows
components.plain: Advances many worlds as one vectorised batch with the checks on the device. The candidate for the one production path.

components.label: One production path
components.plain: Naming one execution path for production and declaring the others as reference paths, with shared admission and checkpoint checks.

components.label: Compile policy
components.plain: A rule for what is compiled into a program and what is passed in, with a budget for compile time and memory.

components.label: Run-view output
components.plain: Every run will save what a viewer needs to replay it: geometry, identities, record metadata, events and how each layer is represented. The requirement is recorded (D154); its design note comes first.

components.label: Device placement
components.plain: Says explicitly whether work runs on a CPU or a GPU.

components.label: Checkpoints and files
components.plain: Saves complete checkpoints, so a run can restart exactly or branch into alternative futures.

components.label: Checkpoint continuity
components.plain: Lets a checkpoint written by one version of the code resume under another, but only through a recorded admission. Refusal stays the default. In place for CPU runs; the GPU extension is being built.

sources.where: Status on 14 November 2026, and the working order (D156)

components.label: Observers
components.plain: Read-only measurements taken from a run. Observing never changes the dynamics.

components.label: Tissue preparation
components.plain: Prepares a tissue before an experiment and hands its full state to the next phase, with no silent re-equilibration.

components.label: Cell removal
components.plain: Cuts cells out of a tissue and continues the run, keeping the surviving material and its history.

components.label: Other core modules
components.plain: Core modules not grouped elsewhere on this map.

components.label: Checked RK4
components.plain: A fixed-step integrator that checks every trial state and refuses a failed step; it never repairs one.

components.label: IMEX step
components.plain: The tissue models' time step, treating the fast electrical part implicitly. It refactorises a dense matrix every step, which limits tissue size.

components.label: Field solvers
components.plain: Solve for the voltages that keep charge consistent across membranes and the space between cells. Limited to 2,048 electrical nodes today.

components.label: Field-solver interface
components.plain: An interface that keeps the field law and its checks while allowing sparse or matrix-free solvers. Proposed, with no code yet.

components.label: Transport kernels
components.plain: Shared array kernels for moving ions across membranes and junctions.

components.label: Gate updates
components.plain: Exact exponential updates for channel gates.

components.label: Water step
components.plain: The numerical step for water flow and volume change.

components.label: Membrane redistribution
components.plain: Moves channels and pumps along the membrane while conserving their number.

components.label: Projective stepping
components.plain: A long-time mode that takes bursts of fine steps and then jumps ahead. It failed its qualification on the absolute error caps.

components.label: Fixed points
components.plain: Finds a tissue's resting states and follows them as parameters change. Passed all 16 criteria of its protocol.

components.label: Long-time methods
components.plain: Multirate or quasi-steady stepping for hours to months of biology. A verdict on them is a deliverable of the compute-limits gate.

components.label: Mechanical analysis
components.plain: Finds mechanical equilibria of a cell sheet and infers junction tensions from its shape. Qualified with the vertex model.

components.label: Other numerics
components.plain: Numerics and analysis modules not grouped elsewhere on this map.

components.label: Membrane transport
components.plain: Ions cross membranes driven by concentration and voltage, with each transfer counted once.

components.label: Channel catalogue
components.plain: 56 sodium, potassium, HCN, calcium and leak channel laws. The heredity channels NaV1.2 and Kir2.1 pass BETSE parity.

sources.where: Parity P4b, the heredity carrier channels

components.label: Pumps
components.plain: The sodium–potassium pump and the calcium pumps, which spend ATP to move ions uphill.

components.label: Gap junctions
components.plain: Gated channels between neighbouring cells, and the law by which a new cell forms its junctions over time.

components.label: Cotransport
components.plain: Carriers that move two kinds of ion together, including the potassium–anion symport cells use to regulate volume.

components.label: Reactions
components.plain: Chemical reactions inside compartments, with mass and energy accounted for.

components.label: Calcium and IP3
components.plain: Calcium release from the ER store, IP3 signalling and calcium entry at the membrane.

components.label: Fuel and mitochondria
components.plain: Finite pools of ATP that pumps draw on, and passive ion exchange with mitochondria. Respiration is not modelled.

components.label: Network regulation
components.plain: Rules that let ion levels and fuel regulate pumps, channels and junctions.

sources.where: Live network regulation of pumps, channels and junctions

components.label: Injury and resealing
components.plain: A membrane injury that leaks ions and reseals on a set schedule.

components.label: Physiological noise
components.plain: Random variation with explicit, repeatable random streams.

components.label: Tissue geometry
components.plain: Builds cells as polygons with explicit volumes, areas and neighbours.

components.label: Extracellular grid
components.plain: A grid for ions and currents in the space around cells.

components.label: Charged-surface backend
components.plain: Array kernels for charge-consistent membrane surfaces.

components.label: Vertex mechanics
components.plain: The forces in a sheet of cells, from edge tension and area elasticity. Topology is fixed: cells cannot yet swap neighbours.

components.label: Topology changes
components.plain: Cells swapping neighbours, leaving the sheet and dividing within it, with ions, charge and energy conserved.

components.label: Coupling out of the inventory
components.plain: A species amount in the inventory sets how available a junction or channel is, so chemistry can change electrical behaviour. The design is accepted (14 November 2026): junctions first, with channels pending. Nothing is implemented yet.

sources.where: The inventory-coupling design (D155 item 1, scoped by D156) is accepted
Status on 14 November 2026, and the working order (D156)

components.label: Excitable tissue
components.plain: General physics for tissue that carries a travelling electrical wave, to be qualified against cable theory. A design note comes first.

sources.where: Status on 14 November 2026, and the working order (D156)

components.label: Gene regulation in tissue
components.plain: Gene networks that set how much of each protein is made, coupled to the tissue's physiology.

sources.where: Where things stand: New biology in the engine

components.label: Golgi and trafficking
components.plain: The pathway that carries new proteins from the ER through the Golgi to the membrane or out of the cell. Planned, not started.

components.label: Other laws
components.plain: Process modules not grouped elsewhere on this map.

components.label: First bounded models
components.plain: The first small models: one cell, a pair, a regulatory circuit and small graphs of cells. Each was accepted in its own bounded scope.

components.label: Finite and spatial exterior
components.plain: Models where the fluid outside cells is a finite, spatial inventory with its own ions and fields.

components.label: Calcium and chemistry
components.plain: Models of calcium stores, IP3 signalling and compartment chemistry, tested on synthetic cases.

components.label: Pump tissue @1–@3
components.plain: The tissue model behind the BETSE comparisons: pumps, channels, junctions and the space between cells. It passes parity on CPU and on the GPU.

components.label: Water and volume
components.plain: The pump tissue with osmotic water, changing cell volume and volume regulation. Now a thin composition of operators.

sources.where: Osmotic water and volume qualified and landed

components.label: Cell replacement
components.plain: The pump tissue with scheduled replacement of cells. Now a thin composition of operators.

components.label: Composite tissue model
components.plain: The newer design: the pump tissue's own step plus declared operators, so new combinations are definitions and not new model modules. Numerically qualified on CPU through its frozen-model guards and judged in E07-v1; agreement on the GPU is in progress.

sources.where: Status on 14 November 2026, and the working order (D156)

components.label: Resolved tissue families
components.plain: The older design: one module for each combination of calcium, fuel, water, repair, profiles and interventions. Kept frozen on purpose.

components.label: Apical vertex model
components.plain: A two-dimensional mechanical model of a cell sheet. It passed 57 of 57 criteria under its second protocol, after the first judged run failed.

components.label: Protein-cage assembly
components.plain: Protein cages forming from folded subunits drawn from finite pools, with an experimental link to cell models. Folding itself is out of scope.

components.label: Other model modules
components.plain: Model modules not grouped elsewhere on this map.

components.label: Coherent cell model
components.plain: One cell in which many processes share the same inventories and predict several measured responses.

components.label: Integrated tissue unit
components.plain: Mechanics, transport and the cell lifecycle together on changing geometry.

components.label: First organ
components.plain: The simplest useful organ, expressed as a data definition. The organ and species are not yet chosen.

components.label: Coupled organs
components.plain: Two or more organs linked through explicit transport and signalling.

components.label: Operator contract
components.plain: What every operator must declare: the state it owns, what it writes and reads, its energy bookings and its conflicts. Checked when a model is built.

sources.where: Status on 14 November 2026, and the working order (D156)

components.label: Endogenous lifecycle
components.plain: Division triggered by a cell's own growth or regulation, with repeated births and deaths. Mitosis itself is further down the road.

components.label: BETSE parity ladder
components.plain: Cells' own physics compared with saved output from the BETSE simulator, one mechanism family at a time. Every family tested so far passes, on CPU and GPU.

components.label: MG0: gradient and wall
components.plain: Two morphogenesis checks: a morphogen gradient and a bistable voltage domain wall. Both passed.

sources.where: MG0a morphogen gradient passes; MG0b bistable domain wall passes

components.label: MG0c: Turing patterns
components.plain: Pattern formation by reaction and diffusion: the qualification of the shared-inventory reactions. In progress.

sources.where: Status on 14 November 2026, and the working order (D156)

components.label: MG1: vertex mechanics
components.plain: Does a mechanical cell sheet relax to known equilibria? Passed on its second protocol, 57 of 57.

components.label: Cell division S2–S5a
components.plain: Prescribed division of the early frog egg, judged against independently written references. Stages through S5a passed.

components.label: E07-v1: renewal
components.plain: Can a voltage pattern written into a tissue survive while its cells are replaced? Judged: under donor-copy turnover it did not renew, and 8 of 15 predictions held.

components.label: E07-v2: write, clear, challenge
components.plain: The follow-up heredity experiment: write a state, clear the cue, then challenge the tissue. Drafted as proposed, awaiting review.

components.label: E15: pattern recovery
components.plain: Which layers restore a pattern after damage, as opposed to only generating it? In the backlog, not active.

components.label: Conduction probe
components.plain: Can the channel laws the composite admits carry an action potential along a chain of cells? A probe on the engine as it stands is in progress, with its success criteria set before it runs.

sources.where: Status on 14 November 2026, and the working order (D156)

components.label: W1: heredity pilot
components.plain: Development runs: a brief cue writes a depolarised disc, and written discs held for 70 minutes, also with water.

components.label: Paper tests
components.plain: Published models to reproduce and test in Cells. Three have test plans; the Cortés-Poza reproduction ran outside the engine.

components.label: Two-task readout
components.plain: Can one tissue trajectory carry both where a cue was and when it came? Further work on it is deferred.

components.label: BETSE v1.5.0
components.plain: An established bioelectric simulator, run unmodified in its own environment. Cells compares against its saved output and never contains its code.

components.label: BITSEY
components.plain: A simplified regulatory and ionic simulator, the reference for the regulation models.

components.label: tyssue
components.plain: A vertex-model library, run out of process as the reference for the mechanics check.

components.label: Asor et al. data
components.plain: Mass-photometry measurements and a stochastic model of protein-cage assembly.

components.label: Protein catalogue
components.plain: A curated list giving each modelled channel, pump and junction a stable identity linked to UniProt, the Human Protein Atlas, PDB and Reactome. Metadata only.

components.label: BETSE comparison tools
components.plain: Runs BETSE out of process, extracts its output and compares Cells against it.

components.label: Tissue and heredity drivers
components.plain: The drivers, scorers and judges for the tissue and heredity experiments.

components.label: Division references
components.plain: Independently written reference solutions for cell division, with the drivers that compare the engine against them.

components.label: Mechanics references
components.plain: Reference solutions and runners for the morphogenesis and mechanics checks.

components.label: Reaction references
components.plain: Reference solutions for the planned reaction operator, written by an agent that never read the operator's code.

components.label: Other validation areas
components.plain: Reference solutions and checks for assembly, channels, chemistry, geometry, transport and more.

components.label: Test tiers gate
components.plain: The routine gate: every test file's outcome is compared with a recorded baseline before code lands.

ideal_osmosis_linear_compliance_water@1.label: Osmotic water
ideal_osmosis_linear_compliance_water@1.plain: Water follows osmotic pressure and cell volumes change. Every other law then sees the new volumes.

sources.where: Osmotic water and volume qualified and landed

k_anion_symport_mass_action@1.label: K–anion symport
k_anion_symport_mass_action@1.plain: A carrier that moves potassium and an anion together, the route by which cells regulate their volume.

sources.where: Osmotic water and volume qualified and landed

scheduled_cell_replacement@1.label: Cell replacement
scheduled_cell_replacement@1.plain: Removes a cell and puts a newcomer in its place on a schedule, with waste, supply and lineage recorded. Newcomers form junctions over time.

scheduled_cell_replacement@2.label: Replacement over water
scheduled_cell_replacement@2.plain: Cell replacement in a tissue whose volumes change: the newcomer brings its own volume, booked in water's accounts. Implemented and guarded; not qualified on the heredity sheet.

sources.where: Status on 14 November 2026, and the working order (D156)

electrode_current_injection@1.label: Current injection
electrode_current_injection@1.plain: Injects current through an electrode, as in an experiment, with the charge and work recorded.

membrane_entity_state@1.label: Membrane state
membrane_entity_state@1.plain: Makes membrane area, capacitance and channel numbers into state that other operators can change.

sources.where: Gate: lifecycle operators, status of 14 November

scheduled_membrane_insertion@1.label: Membrane insertion
scheduled_membrane_insertion@1.plain: Adds new membrane to a patch at a scheduled rate, as a dividing egg does.

restricted_cleft_lumen@1.label: Cleft lumen
restricted_cleft_lumen@1.plain: A small enclosed space between cells that fills with fluid as it grows.

isopotential_partition@1.label: Partition
isopotential_partition@1.plain: Divides a cell into two daughters, splitting its ions, membrane and channels with every account closed.

cytoplasmic_bridge_closure@1.label: Bridge closure
cytoplasmic_bridge_closure@1.plain: Closes the cytoplasmic bridge that still joins two daughters after division.

scheduled_membrane_insertion@2.label: Membrane insertion @2
scheduled_membrane_insertion@2.plain: Membrane insertion in the form division uses, where new patches open during the run.

restricted_cleft_lumen@2.label: Cleft lumen @2
restricted_cleft_lumen@2.plain: The cleft lumen in the form division uses, faced by several membrane patches.

scheduled_species_turnover@1.label: Species turnover
scheduled_species_turnover@1.plain: Production and clearance of secreted molecules, inside cells and between them. Implemented and guarded. Its first-order clearance is part of the numerically qualified secreted-species transport (D150 v1); production is guarded by tests only.

scheduled_species_exchange@1.label: Species exchange
scheduled_species_exchange@1.plain: Secretion and uptake of molecules across the membrane. Implemented and guarded: it entered the D150 v1 qualification only through its guard tests, so it is not yet qualified.

sources.where: Secreted-species transport (D150 v1) is numerically qualified

local_species_reactions@1.label: Shared-inventory reactions
local_species_reactions@1.plain: Reactions between species in the tissue's one inventory, with exact energy bookings. Development code with no judged run; its qualification, MG0c, is in progress.

sources.where: Reactions on the shared inventory (D152 v1), milestones 1 and 2, landed

shared_state.heading: The central abstraction: shared physical state
shared_state.note: From the ownership contract that the composition gate is making explicit. The plan records no status for each entity.

plain.Compartment: A volume holding material: the amounts of each species, the volume itself and its fixed charge.
plain.Membrane domain: A patch of membrane with its area, capacitance, position and orientation.
plain.Functional-unit population: A population of one kind of channel, pump or other unit: what it is, how many there are and their internal state.
plain.Contact: A contact between two cells: its endpoints, geometry, junction abundance and gate state.
plain.Cell and lineage: A cell's stable identity, its membership and its ancestry.
plain.Extracellular environment: The space outside cells, with its own material, geometry and boundary conditions.

today's commitments.label: Today's commitments
today's commitments.plain: Land the composite, the plan-validation fix, the neutral renaming and the division diagnostic before any new track starts.
today's commitments.note: The plan records no closing status. PROGRESS records all four landings on 12 and 13 November.

execution.label: Execution
execution.plain: Make execution dependable: fast plan validation, live progress markers, one production path and a compile policy.
execution.note: The plan-validation fix was accepted on 12 November; phase-marker completion records are implemented. One production path, the compile policy and the registry are not started; the run-view output's design is pending (the plan, 14 November).

composition.label: Composition
composition.plain: One composite physiology model with an explicit contract for who owns and who writes each piece of state.
composition.note: From the plan, 14 November: secreted-species version 1 is implemented and guarded, with its protocol registered; the reactions operator's milestones 1 and 2 have landed, and MG0c, its qualification, is in progress.

lifecycle operators.label: Lifecycle operators
lifecycle operators.plain: The operations of cell division: membrane state, insertion, a restricted compartment, current injection, partition and bridge closure.
lifecycle operators.note: From the plan, 14 November: membrane state, insertion, the lumen, current injection and S5a's operators are qualified. S5b and the endogenous lifecycle come later; J2 and C1 stay held.

compute limits.label: Compute limits
compute limits.plain: Measure where the cost goes, measure the GH200, define a field-solver interface and reach a verdict on long-time methods.
compute limits.note: A field-solver interface was proposed on 13 November, with no code (PROGRESS). GH200 measurements wait for access.

coupled renewal.label: Coupled renewal
coupled renewal.plain: The heredity question: can a written state repeatedly renew as cells are replaced?
coupled renewal.note: From the plan, 14 November: E07-v1 is judged, and under donor-copy turnover the written disc did not renew. E07-v2 is drafted as proposed.

a closed molecular-to-physiology loop.label: Molecular-to-physiology loop
a closed molecular-to-physiology loop.plain: One regulated population of channels or junctions, from production through assembly and trafficking to a measured physiological response, in one material account.
a closed molecular-to-physiology loop.note: The plan records no status. The unit is provisionally the junction-channel population (D145).

an integrated tissue unit.label: Integrated tissue unit
an integrated tissue unit.plain: Mechanics, transport and the lifecycle together on changing geometry.

capabilities.label: Membrane voltage
capabilities.plain: Ions cross the membrane and set its voltage, with every ion, charge and joule accounted for. Checked against the BETSE simulator.

capabilities.label: Ion channels
capabilities.plain: Channels open and close with the membrane voltage. Each kind is a population with gates, not individual proteins. The catalogue holds 56 laws. NaV1.2 and Kir2.1, the channels the heredity experiments use, pass the BETSE comparison; channel time constants are still open.

sources.where: Parity P4b, the heredity carrier channels
Where things stand: Checking the physics against BETSE

capabilities.label: Ion pumps
capabilities.plain: The sodium–potassium pump and calcium pumps move ions uphill and spend ATP. Each is a population with a rate law. The calcium pump's comparison passed on a second protocol, after the first failed on one item.

capabilities.label: Gap junctions
capabilities.plain: Neighbouring cells exchange ions through gated junctions, and a new cell forms its junctions over time.

capabilities.label: Space between cells
capabilities.plain: The fluid around cells holds its own ions and electric fields, with barriers between regions.

sources.where: Parity rungs P2 and P4 pass

capabilities.label: Water and cell volume
capabilities.plain: Water follows osmotic pressure, so cells swell, shrink and regulate their volume.

sources.where: Osmotic water and volume qualified and landed

capabilities.label: Calcium and the ER
capabilities.plain: Calcium moves between the cytoplasm and the ER store, with IP3-triggered release. Tested on synthetic cases.

capabilities.label: Fuel (ATP)
capabilities.plain: Pumps draw on a finite pool of ATP that has to be regenerated. In the composite model fuel is held constant.

capabilities.label: Mitochondria
capabilities.plain: Mitochondria exchange ions with the cytoplasm and carry their own voltage. Respiration and ATP synthesis are not modelled.

capabilities.label: Regulatory circuits
capabilities.plain: Small gene circuits that switch a cell between states, alone or in a two-cell model.

sources.where: What Cells can do: Regulatory cell state

capabilities.label: Gene regulation in tissue
capabilities.plain: Gene networks that set how much of each protein is made, coupled to the tissue. Planned.

sources.where: Where things stand: New biology in the engine

capabilities.label: Golgi and trafficking
capabilities.plain: New proteins would pass from the ER through the Golgi to the membrane or out of the cell. Planned, not started.

capabilities.label: Protein assembly
capabilities.plain: Protein cages build up from folded subunits drawn from a finite pool. Assembly is modelled as bonds forming and breaking, not as molecules moving in space. Folding is out of scope.

capabilities.label: Molecular machines
capabilities.plain: Larger machines such as the proteasome. A goal: they will mostly be modelled in aggregate and drawn as illustrations.

capabilities.label: Cell chemistry
capabilities.plain: Chemical reactions inside compartments, with mass and energy accounted for. Reactions on the tissue's shared inventory are implemented and guarded; their qualification is in progress.

capabilities.label: Secreted signals
capabilities.plain: Signalling molecules spread between cells and are cleared. That transport and clearance are numerically qualified in the composite model, with a held source (D150 v1). Release, uptake and production are implemented and guarded by tests, not yet qualified.

sources.where: Secreted-species transport (D150 v1) is numerically qualified

capabilities.label: Injury and repair
capabilities.plain: A membrane injury leaks ions and reseals. The resealing follows a set schedule.

capabilities.label: Cell division
capabilities.plain: A cell divides into two daughters on a set schedule, splitting its contents, membrane and channels with closed accounts. Division triggered by the cell itself is planned.

capabilities.label: Cell replacement
capabilities.plain: Cells are removed and replaced on a schedule, and newcomers form junctions over time. This is how the heredity experiments turn a tissue over.

capabilities.label: Tissue mechanics
capabilities.plain: Cells in a sheet pull on their shared edges and relax to mechanical equilibrium. Cells cannot yet swap neighbours.

capabilities.label: Cell sheets
capabilities.plain: A sheet of 127 coupled cells runs on ordinary processors today; the judged heredity experiment E07-v1 used it. The full tissue of 825 electrical nodes needs faster hardware or a long-time method.

sources.where: Gate: coupled renewal, 'Scale is named, not assumed'

scales.label: Molecules
scales.plain: Channels, pumps and protein cages are modelled as populations and counts, not atom by atom. Shapes drawn at this scale are illustrations.
scales.note: Assembly from prefolded proteins is mostly modelled, not simulated physically.

scales.label: One cell
scales.plain: The current focus: a coherent model of one cell, where many processes share the same inventories.

scales.label: Tissue
scales.plain: Sheets of coupled cells run today. An integrated tissue unit with mechanics and the lifecycle is a later gate.

scales.label: Organ
scales.plain: A first whole organ, defined as data. Planned; the organ and species are not yet chosen.

scales.label: Whole organism
scales.plain: Interacting organ systems, and in time whole animals. A long-term goal; nothing is built.

relation_kinds.label: uses
relation_kinds.description: The first part imports the second in the source code.

relation_kinds.label: is an operator of
relation_kinds.description: Registered as an operator of the composite model.

relation_kinds.label: requires
relation_kinds.description: The operator declares that this law must come before it.

relation_kinds.label: writes
relation_kinds.description: The operator declares that it changes this state and books the change.

relation_kinds.label: provides
relation_kinds.description: The operator provides this state to the rest of the model as its current value.

relation_kinds.label: reads
